1	// Andes-CSR capability gating.
2	//
3	// A core implements an Andes custom CSR only when the matching feature is
4	// configured into it (config.inc). Restoring a CSR the target core lacks can
5	// hang the DMI handshake -- observed on ax45mpv_premium for ucode (no DSP) and
6	// mecc_code (no ECC). So the resume/drain loops transport only the CSRs the
7	// target core supports, decided here from the core's feature gates.
8	//
9	// This header is Verilator/SystemC-free: it maps a CSR address to its gate and
10	// answers "does a core with these gates support this CSR". The binding of each
11	// gate to the core's compiled-in `_NDS_*` config macros lives in the sim binary
12	// (see andes_caps_from_config), so this stays unit-testable in isolation.
13	#ifndef ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
14	#define ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
15	
16	#include <cstdint>
17	#include <string>
18	#include <vector>
19	
20	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
21	
22	namespace hybrid {
23	
24	// The hardware feature that gates each Andes CSR. ALWAYS = unconditionally
25	// present (a base Andes V5 machine CSR every core has; never gated off).
26	enum class AndesGate : uint8_t {
27	  ALWAYS = 0,
28	  DSP,
29	  CODENSE,
30	  POWERBRAKE,
31	  STACKSAFE,
32	  ECC,
33	  PMA,
34	  ILM,
35	  DLM,
36	  PERF_MONITOR,
37	};
38	
39	// Map an Andes CSR (by address) to the feature gate that enables it. Addresses
40	// are the HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST scalars plus the PMA block. A CSR with no
41	// custom-extension gate is ALWAYS (a base machine CSR every Andes core has).
42	// Maintainer note: a CSR added to HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST that needs gating must
43	// get a case here, else it defaults to ALWAYS (transported unconditionally).
44	constexpr AndesGate andes_gate_for(uint16_t csr_addr)
45	{
46	  switch (csr_addr) {
47	    case 0x801: return AndesGate::DSP;           // ucode (DSP overflow flag)
48	    case 0x800: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // uitb  (CoDense table base)
49	    case 0x017: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // jvt   (Zcmt/CoDense)
50	    case 0x7C5: return AndesGate::POWERBRAKE;     // mpft_ctl
51	    case 0x7C2: return AndesGate::ECC;            // mecc_code
52	    case 0x7C6:                                   // mhsp_ctl
53	    case 0x7C7:                                   // msp_bound
54	    case 0x7C8: return AndesGate::STACKSAFE;      // msp_base
55	    case 0x7C0: return AndesGate::ILM;            // milmb (ILM base)
56	    case 0x7C1: return AndesGate::DLM;            // mdlmb (DLM base)
57	    case 0x7D1: return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;   // mcountermask_m
58	    default:
59	      // PMA cfg (0xBC0, 0xBC2) and addr (0xBD0..0xBDF) blocks.
60	      if (csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR || csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2)
61	        return AndesGate::PMA;
62	      if (csr_addr >= HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR &&
63	          csr_addr < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM)
64	        return AndesGate::PMA;
65	      return AndesGate::ALWAYS;                    // mxstatus 0x7C4, mclk_ctl 0x7DF
66	  }
67	}
68	
69	// The set of Andes feature gates a target core has on. Built from the core's
70	// compiled-in config (config.inc) in the sim binary and injected into the
71	// resume/drain loops, so they transport only the CSRs the core implements.
72	// Default = every gate on (all(): no gating, the prior unconditional behavior).
73	struct AndesCaps {
74	  uint32_t gate_mask = ~0u;
75	
76	  static constexpr AndesCaps all()  { return AndesCaps{~0u}; }
77	  static constexpr AndesCaps none() { return AndesCaps{0u}; }
78	
79	  constexpr void set(AndesGate g, bool on = true)
80	  {
81	    const uint32_t bit = 1u << static_cast<unsigned>(g);
82	    if (on) gate_mask |= bit;
83	    else    gate_mask &= ~bit;
84	  }
85	
86	  constexpr bool gate_on(AndesGate g) const
87	  {
88	    return (gate_mask >> static_cast<unsigned>(g)) & 1u;
89	  }
90	
91	  // ALWAYS-gated CSRs are present on every core regardless of the mask.
92	  constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const
93	  {
94	    const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);
95	    return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);
96	  }
97	};
98	
99	// The Andes scalar CSR names this core supports, for the --describe card.
100	// Iterates HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST (the single source of truth for the set).
101	inline std::vector<std::string> supported_andes_csr_names(const AndesCaps& caps)
102	{
103	  std::vector<std::string> out;
104	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
105	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
106	#undef X
107	  // PMA group markers (whole pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] blocks share one gate), so a
108	  // consumer can include/exclude PMA without listing all 18 entries.
109	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR))  out.push_back("pmacfg");
110	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR)) out.push_back("pmaaddr");
111	  return out;
112	}
113	
114	}  // namespace hybrid
115	
116	#endif  // ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
117

1	// Build an AndesCaps from the core's compiled-in config.inc feature macros
2	// (_NDS_*, supplied by the build-generated cpu_config.hpp). This is the ONE
3	// place that binds each Andes feature gate to its config macro -- the sim-binary
4	// counterpart of the Verilator-free andes_caps.hpp, kept separate so the unit
5	// tests never need the generated header.
6	//
7	// PRECONDITION: the _NDS_* macros must already be in scope (include this AFTER
8	// cpu_config.hpp). A macro that is absent reads as "feature off" (gate clear),
9	// never a compile error -- so a core whose config omits a knob stays safe.
10	#pragma once
11	
12	#include "hybrid/andes_caps.hpp"
13	
14	namespace hybrid {
15	
16	inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config()
17	{
18	  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();
19	
20	#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
21	  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);           // ucode
22	#endif
23	#if defined(_NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT
24	  c.set(AndesGate::CODENSE);       // uitb, jvt
25	#endif
26	#if defined(_NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT
27	  c.set(AndesGate::POWERBRAKE);    // mpft_ctl
28	#endif
29	#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
30	  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);     // mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base
31	#endif
32	#if defined(_NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT) && _NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT
33	  c.set(AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR);  // mcountermask_m
34	#endif
35	#if defined(_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES) && (_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES > 0)
36	  c.set(AndesGate::PMA);           // pmacfg / pmaaddr
37	#endif
38	#if defined(_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB > 0)
39	  c.set(AndesGate::ILM);           // milmb
40	#endif
41	#if defined(_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB > 0)
42	  c.set(AndesGate::DLM);           // mdlmb
43	#endif
44	  // ECC: mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC.
45	#if (defined(_NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
46	    (defined(_NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
47	    (defined(_NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    || \
48	    (defined(_NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)
49	  c.set(AndesGate::ECC);           // mecc_code
50	#endif
51	
52	  return c;
53	}
54	
55	}  // namespace hybrid

#

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

DERIVE="$ROOT/tools/cpu_config_to_march_converter/scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py"
[ -f "$DERIVE" ] || fail "missing deriver: $DERIVE"

VSIM_BIN_DIR="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/../vsim_andesim/build}"
ENG="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium"

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Derive the andesim hybrid Andes-CSR capability list from a core's config.inc.
3	
4	This is the OFFLINE checker for the andesim hybrid handoff. It mirrors, in
5	Python, the C++ gate logic the vsim engine compiles in
6	(src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp + andes_caps_config.hpp). At runtime the engine
7	reports the same list via `sim_<core> --describe` ("andes_csrs"), and the
8	andesim driver uses it to skip --verify on CSRs the engine lacks. Running this
9	on the same config.inc must produce the same list -- a drift guard between the
10	offline config and the built engine (the flywheel).
11	
12	Each Andes CSR is gated by a config.inc feature: a core implements the CSR only
13	when its feature is configured in. Restoring/draining a CSR the core lacks can
14	hang the DM handshake, so the engine and this checker gate on the same map.
15	
16	Usage:
17	  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py <config.inc>                       # print the list
18	  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py --check <config.inc> <csr> [csr...]  # assert exact
19	"""
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import sys
23	from pathlib import Path
24	
25	sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
26	from config_to_march import _int, is_yes, parse_inc  # noqa: E402
27	
28

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Derive the andesim hybrid Andes-CSR capability list from a core's config.inc.

This is the OFFLINE checker for the andesim hybrid handoff. It mirrors, in
Python, the C++ gate logic the vsim engine compiles in
(src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp + andes_caps_config.hpp). At runtime the engine
reports the same list via `sim_<core> --describe` ("andes_csrs"), and the
andesim driver uses it to skip --verify on CSRs the engine lacks. Running this
on the same config.inc must produce the same list -- a drift guard between the
offline config and the built engine (the flywheel).

Each Andes CSR is gated by a config.inc feature: a core implements the CSR only
when its feature is configured in. Restoring/draining a CSR the core lacks can
hang the DM handshake, so the engine and this checker gate on the same map.

Usage:
  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py <config.inc>                       # print the list
  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py --check <config.inc> <csr> [csr...]  # assert exact
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from config_to_march import _int, is_yes, parse_inc  # noqa: E402


def _ecc_any(cfg: dict) -> bool:
    """mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC (type != none)."""
    for blk in ("NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE", "NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE",
                "NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE", "NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE"):
        n = _int(cfg, blk)
        if n is not None and n > 0:
            return True
    return False


def gates(cfg: dict) -> dict:
    """Feature gates, mirroring andes_caps_from_config() in the vsim binary."""
    return {
        "DSP":          is_yes(cfg, "NDS_DSP_SUPPORT"),
        "CODENSE":      is_yes(cfg, "NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT"),
        "POWERBRAKE":   is_yes(cfg, "NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT"),
        "STACKSAFE":    is_yes(cfg, "NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT"),
        "PERF_MONITOR": is_yes(cfg, "NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR"),
        "PMA":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_PMA_ENTRIES") or 0) > 0,
        "ILM":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "DLM":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "ECC":          _ecc_any(cfg),
        "ALWAYS":       True,
    }


# (csr name, gate) in HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST order, then the PMA group markers --
# mirrors andes_caps.hpp andes_gate_for() + supported_andes_csr_names().
_CSR_GATES = [
    ("mxstatus",       "ALWAYS"),
    ("mpft_ctl",       "POWERBRAKE"),
    ("mclk_ctl",       "ALWAYS"),
    ("milmb",          "ILM"),
    ("mdlmb",          "DLM"),
    ("mecc_code",      "ECC"),
    ("mhsp_ctl",       "STACKSAFE"),
    ("msp_bound",      "STACKSAFE"),
    ("msp_base",       "STACKSAFE"),
    ("mcountermask_m", "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("uitb",           "CODENSE"),
    ("jvt",            "CODENSE"),
    ("ucode",          "DSP"),
    ("pmacfg",         "PMA"),
    ("pmaaddr",        "PMA"),
]


def supported_andes_csrs(cfg: dict) -> list:
    g = gates(cfg)
    return [name for name, gate in _CSR_GATES if g[gate]]


def main(argv: list) -> int:
    if argv and argv[0] == "--check":
        if len(argv) < 2:
            print(__doc__)
            return 2
        got = supported_andes_csrs(parse_inc(Path(argv[1])))
        want = argv[2:]
        if got != want:
            print(f"MISMATCH\n  got:  {got}\n  want: {want}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print("OK: " + " ".join(got))
        return 0
    if len(argv) != 1:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    print(" ".join(supported_andes_csrs(parse_inc(Path(argv[0])))))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Convert an Andes `config.inc` file into a versioned RISC-V `-march` string.

Mirrors the canonical `constraint NDS_ISA_STRING { ... }` block from
`config_tool/ax46mpv-nds-softcore-config.tcl` line-by-line so the output is
byte-identical to the `NDS_ISA_STRING` macro that the TCL `gen_config` would
embed in a config.inc.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/config_to_march.py <file.inc> [<file2.inc> ...]
    python3 scripts/config_to_march.py --check config_inc/*.inc
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Matches:  `define NAME    value     // optional comment
DEFINE_RE = re.compile(r'^\s*`define\s+(\w+)(?:\s+(.+?))?\s*(?://\s*(.*))?$')


# ---------- parsing -----------------------------------------------------------

def parse_inc(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {macro: string-value}, normalising the four observed formats.

    Resolution order per macro:
      1. quoted string  -> string
      2. numeric + `// symbolic` comment  -> the comment text
      3. integer literal alone -> the integer as a string
    Also captures any `_INT` companion macro and the embedded NDS_ISA_STRING.
    """
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
        m = DEFINE_RE.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        name = m.group(1)
        raw = (m.group(2) or "").strip().rstrip(",")
        comment = (m.group(3) or "").strip()

        if not raw:
            # bare `define NAME (used like a flag)
            out.setdefault(name, "1")
            continue

        if raw.startswith('"') and raw.endswith('"'):
            out[name] = raw[1:-1]
            continue

        # Numeric — prefer trailing `// symbolic` comment if present
        c = comment.strip().strip('"')
        if c and " " not in c:
            out[name] = c
            # also keep the integer under the _INT slot if not set
            try:
                int(raw, 0)
                out.setdefault(name + "_INT", raw)
            except ValueError:
                pass
            continue

        # Bare integer (or unparseable token) — store as-is
        out[name] = raw
    return out


# ---------- accessor helpers --------------------------------------------------

def _str(cfg: dict, key: str) -> str:
    """Best-effort string view of a macro, falling back to _INT decoding."""
    if key in cfg:
        return cfg[key].strip().strip('"')
    if key + "_INT" in cfg:
        return cfg[key + "_INT"].strip()
    return ""


def _int(cfg: dict, key: str) -> int | None:
    """Numeric view: prefer the explicit _INT macro, else parse the value."""
    for k in (key + "_INT", key):
        if k in cfg:
            try:
                return int(cfg[k], 0)
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return None


def is_yes(cfg: dict, key: str) -> bool:
    """Mirror Tcl `[selected X] == "yes"` for both quoted and _INT forms."""
    s = _str(cfg, key).lower()
    if s in ("yes", "true", "on"):
        return True
    if s in ("no", "false", "off", ""):
        return False
    n = _int(cfg, key)
    return n is not None and n == 1

* **external** -- the customer-facing snake_case knobs documented in

"""

import sys

from config_inc_shared import (  # noqa: E402
    derive_cpu_model_from_path,
    load_cpu_inc_model,
    parse_verilog_int,
)

    MMSC_CFG_FIELDS,
    MRVARCH_CFG_FIELDS,
    build as build_csr,
    format_diff,
    summary as csr_summary,
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CPU-model -> Alioth IP name.  The external `cores` key requires the IP name
# be one of Alioth's supported set; d23 maps to d23v, etc.  Cores not in this
# table are still emitted (config.inc is authoritative) but flagged on stderr.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
ALIOTH_IP = {
    "ax45mp": "ax45mp",
    "ax46mp": "ax46mp",
    "ax46mpv": "ax46mpv",
    "ax46se": "ax46se",
    "ax46-se": "ax46se",
    "a46mp": "a46mp",
    "a46mpv": "a46mpv",
    "nx45v": "nx45v",
    "d23": "d23v",
    "d23v": "d23v",
    "ax50mpv": "ax50mpv",
    "a50mpv": "a50mpv",
}

# IPs whose external schema exposes ACE knobs.  For others (e.g. d23v, nx45v)
# the `support_ace` key does not exist, so it is never emitted there.
ACE_CAPABLE_IPS = {
    "ax45mp", "ax46mp", "ax46mpv", "ax46se",
    "a46mp", "a46mpv", "ax50mpv", "a50mpv",
}

# IPs that split the local-memory subordinate-port toggle into separate
# ilm/dlm keys instead of the combined `support_lm_subordinate_port`.
SPLIT_LM_SUBPORT_IPS = {"d23v"}

# Shared-cache external key name per IP (the 46-family uses cm500, ax45mp/nx45v
# use l2c500).  None => the IP has no shared-cache external knob (e.g. d23v).
# IPs absent from the table fall back to the generic "l2c500".
SHARED_CACHE_KEY = {
    "ax45mp": "l2c500", "nx45v": "l2c500",
    "a46mp": "cm500", "a46mpv": "cm500", "ax46mp": "cm500", "ax46mpv": "cm500",
    "ax50mpv": "cm500", "a50mpv": "cm500",
    "ax46se": None, "d23v": None,

    "mrvarch_cfg": 0x1F00F,

        if self.has_b:
            bits |= 1 << _MISA_BIT["B"]
        if self.has_c:
            bits |= 1 << _MISA_BIT["C"]
        if self.has_f:
            bits |= 1 << _MISA_BIT["F"]
        if self.has_d:
            bits |= 1 << _MISA_BIT["D"]
        # X = Andes custom extensions; set on every Andes softcore.
        bits |= 1 << _MISA_BIT["X"]
        # MXL: rv32 -> 1, rv64 -> 2, in the top two XLEN bits.
        mxl = 2 if self.is_rv64 else 1
        bits |= mxl << (self.xlen - 2)
        return bits

    def marchid(self) -> int | None:
        if self.cpuid is None:
            return None
        # marchid: top bit set | (CPU ID low bits).
        return (1 << (self.xlen - 1)) | (self.cpuid & 0xFFFF)


def _infer_cores(path: Path) -> int:
    """Infer core count from a filename suffix like '-4c' / '-8c' / '-2c'."""
    import re
    m = re.search(r"-(\d+)c", path.name)
    if m:
        return int(m.group(1))
    return 1


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# YAML emission (flat, ordered, with comments)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
class Block:
    def __init__(self):
        self.lines: list[str] = []

    def comment(self, text: str):
        self.lines.append(f"# {text}")

    def blank(self):
        self.lines.append("")

    def kv(self, key: str, value):
        self.lines.append(f"{key}: {value}")

    def text(self) -> str:
        return "\n".join(self.lines).rstrip() + "\n"


def emit_external(d: CpuDesc) -> str:
    b = Block()
    b.comment(f"Alioth external (customer) config -- generated from {d.path.name}")
    b.comment(f"march={d.march}  ip={d.ip}  xlen={d.xlen}")
    b.comment("config.inc is authoritative for CPU options.")
    b.blank()

    cluster = "top.cluster"
    b.comment("--- cluster general ---")
    b.kv(f"{cluster}.general.cores", ", ".join(d.core_names))
    if d.bus_width is not None:
        b.kv(f"{cluster}.general.bus_data_width", d.bus_width)
    b.kv(f"{cluster}.general.support_hvm", _yaml_bool(d.support_hvm))
    if d.support_hvm:
        b.kv(f"{cluster}.general.hvm.size", _kb_to_size(d.hvm_kb))
        if d.hvm_base is not None:
            b.kv(f"{cluster}.general.hvm.base_addr", f"0x{d.hvm_base:x}")
        if d.hvm_banks is not None:
            b.kv(f"{cluster}.general.hvm.bank_num", d.hvm_banks)
    # shared cache: external key name varies by IP family (cm500 vs l2c500).
    sc = SHARED_CACHE_KEY.get(d.ip, "l2c500")
    if d.l2c_kb is not None and sc is not None:
        b.kv(f"{cluster}.general.{sc}.size", _kb_to_size(d.l2c_kb))
        if d.l2c_base is not None:
            b.kv(f"{cluster}.general.{sc}.base_addr", f"0x{d.l2c_base:x}")
        if d.l2c_banks is not None:
            b.kv(f"{cluster}.general.{sc}.bank_num", d.l2c_banks)
    b.blank()

    for core in d.core_names:
        pfx = f"{cluster}.{core}"
        b.comment(f"--- core {core} ---")
        b.kv(f"{pfx}.fpu_type", d.fpu)
        if d.paddr_width is not None:

        if d.pma_entries is not None:
            b.kv(f"{pfx}.pma_entry_num", d.pma_entries)
        b.kv(f"{pfx}.hart_ids", d.core_names.index(core))
        # caches
        if d.icache_kb is not None:
            b.kv(f"{pfx}.icache.size", _kb_to_size(d.icache_kb))
        if d.dcache_kb is not None:
            b.kv(f"{pfx}.dcache.size", _kb_to_size(d.dcache_kb))
        if d.dcache_mshr is not None:
            b.kv(f"{pfx}.dcache.mshr_num", d.dcache_mshr)
        # local memory
        b.kv(f"{pfx}.support_ilm", _yaml_bool(d.support_ilm))
        if d.support_ilm:
            b.kv(f"{pfx}.ilm.size", _kb_to_size(d.ilm_kb))
            if d.ilm_base is not None:
                b.kv(f"{pfx}.ilm.base_addr_init_value", f"0x{d.ilm_base:x}")
        b.kv(f"{pfx}.support_dlm", _yaml_bool(d.support_dlm))
        if d.support_dlm:
            b.kv(f"{pfx}.dlm.size", _kb_to_size(d.dlm_kb))
            if d.dlm_base is not None:
                b.kv(f"{pfx}.dlm.base_addr_init_value", f"0x{d.dlm_base:x}")

        # for IPs whose schema uses the split form (e.g. d23v).

            b.kv(f"{pfx}.support_dlm_subordinate_port", _yaml_bool(d.slave_port))
        else:
            b.kv(f"{pfx}.support_lm_subordinate_port", _yaml_bool(d.slave_port))

        # ace.* block when ACE is actually enabled in config.inc.
        if d.support_ace or d.ip in ACE_CAPABLE_IPS:

def _mmsc_sources(d: CpuDesc) -> dict:
    """Map mmsc_cfg field source-keys to (value, source-label)."""
    return {
        "ecc": d.ecc, "ecc@src": "cfg:NDS_*_ECC_TYPE",
        "tlb_ecc": d.tlb_ecc, "tlb_ecc@src": "cfg:NDS_STLB_ECC_TYPE",
        "codense": int(d.codense), "codense@src": "cfg:NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT",
        "powerbrake": int(d.powerbrake), "powerbrake@src": "cfg:NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT",
        "ace": int(d.support_ace), "ace@src": "cfg:NDS_ACE_SUPPORT",
        "vplic": int(d.vplic), "vplic@src": "cfg:NDS_VECTOR_PLIC_SUPPORT",
        "perf": int(d.perf), "perf@src": "march:xandesperf",
        "slaveport": int(d.slave_port), "slaveport@src": "cfg:NDS_SLAVE_PORT_SUPPORT",
        "dsp": int(d.dsp), "dsp@src": "cfg:NDS_DSP_SUPPORT",
        "ppma": int(d.ppma), "ppma@src": "cfg:NDS_PMA_ENTRIES",
    }


def derive_csrs(d: CpuDesc, alioth_dir: Path | None):
    """Compute spec-derived mmsc_cfg / mrvarch_cfg plus their reference values
    and per-field diffs.  The reference is the per-core iss file when present,
    else the generic Alioth base constant (ACE variant when ACE is on)."""
    ref_iss = _load_iss_reference(alioth_dir, d.ip) if alioth_dir else None

    def _ref(key: str, default: int) -> int:
        if ref_iss and key in ref_iss:
            try:
                return int(ref_iss[key], 0)
            except ValueError:
                pass
        return default

    mmsc_ref = _ref("iss.mmsc_cfg", _ACE_MMSC_CFG if d.support_ace else _BASE_CSR["mmsc_cfg"])
    mrvarch_ref = _ref("iss.mrvarch_cfg", _BASE_CSR["mrvarch_cfg"])
    # mrvarch_cfg.Zbk (bit 12) covers the Zbk* crypto family (Zbkb/Zbkc/Zbkx),
    # which appear as separate march tokens; alias them to a single "zbk".
    mrvarch_tokens = set(d.tokens)
    if any(t.startswith("zbk") for t in d.tokens):
        mrvarch_tokens.add("zbk")
    mmsc_val, mmsc_diffs = build_csr(MMSC_CFG_FIELDS, _mmsc_sources(d), frozenset(), mmsc_ref)
    mrvarch_val, mrvarch_diffs = build_csr(MRVARCH_CFG_FIELDS, {}, frozenset(mrvarch_tokens), mrvarch_ref)
    return {
        "mmsc": (mmsc_val, mmsc_ref, mmsc_diffs),
        "mrvarch": (mrvarch_val, mrvarch_ref, mrvarch_diffs),
    }


def emit_internal(d: CpuDesc, alioth_dir: Path | None = None) -> str:
    b = Block()
    b.comment(f"Alioth internal iss config -- generated from {d.path.name}")
    b.comment(f"march={d.march}  ip={d.ip}  xlen={d.xlen}")
    b.comment("misa / marchid / xlen / vlen / elen / mmu / isa_* are derived.")
    b.comment("mmsc_cfg / mrvarch_cfg are SPA-spec bit-derived (primary), with the")
    b.comment("Alioth reference value + changed-field summary shown alongside.")
    b.comment("mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl remain Alioth base reference values.")
    b.blank()

    csrs = derive_csrs(d, alioth_dir)
    mmsc_val, mmsc_ref, mmsc_diffs = csrs["mmsc"]
    mrvarch_val, mrvarch_ref, mrvarch_diffs = csrs["mrvarch"]

    b.kv("iss.misa", f"0x{d.misa():x}")
    march = d.marchid()
    if march is not None:
        b.kv("iss.marchid", f"0x{march:x}")
    b.kv("iss.mvendorid", f"0x{MVENDORID:x}")
    b.kv("iss.mcache_ctl", f"0x{_BASE_CSR['mcache_ctl']:x}")
    b.lines.append(f"iss.mmsc_cfg: 0x{mmsc_val:x}        # spec-derived; reference 0x{mmsc_ref:x}")
    b.comment(f"  mmsc_cfg vs ref: {csr_summary(mmsc_diffs)}")
    b.lines.append(f"iss.mrvarch_cfg: 0x{mrvarch_val:x}     # spec-derived; reference 0x{mrvarch_ref:x}")
    b.comment(f"  mrvarch_cfg vs ref: {csr_summary(mrvarch_diffs)}")
    b.kv("iss.mmisc_ctl", f"0x{_BASE_CSR['mmisc_ctl']:x}")
    b.blank()

    b.kv("iss.xlen", d.xlen)

    ("ESLEEP", 24, 1, None),
